candidates.title: Governance for AI agents running open models: how do you track runs and costs?

When agents run on open models via local runtimes, governance often gets ignored: who ran what, on which model, and at what token cost.

I’m working on a setup (Sharkly.ai, disclosure: I work on it) where every agent run logs its model, trigger source, responsible person and token usage.

Questions:

  • Do you log the model and version per agent run for reproducibility?
  • Are there open tools or standards for agent audit logs that you’d recommend?

candidates.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress on visual reasoning, yet many tasks require evidence that is difficult to obtain through internal reasoning alone: our controlled study on 22 benchmarks shows that simply increasing the inference budget of the base model yields only modest gains. Such tasks demand grounded perception, external knowledge, and numerical measurements obtained through heterogeneous tools, whose outputs must be made interpretable to the model and retained across reasoning steps. candidates.title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
candidates.summary: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable task-level supervision, yet offers limited guidance for localizing errors in visual reasoning. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) complements this supervision with dense token-level corrections from a privileged teacher equipped with an evidence-centered visual view. However, the resulting corrections may conflate visual evidence with non-visual shifts induced by linguistic priors, response style, or the privileged view itself. candidates.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
candidates.summary: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. candidates.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
candidates.summary: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2$\times$ less pretraining compute. candidates.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
candidates.summary: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision.
